title: Depot history, halved
instruction: Rewrite the passage below in no more than 55 words. Output only the rewritten passage, nothing else.
source: The Pennington Street depot opened in 1911 as the northern yard of Harrowgate & Fenwick Tramways. Its first manager, Ailsa Okonkwo-Reyes, stayed until 1934, longer than any of her successors, and is credited with the decision to keep the No. 7 route running through the winter of 1926 when the company's other lines were suspended. The depot's second shed, added along Caldbeck Lane, was never electrified and served as a store for spare bogies. After the tramways closed, the site became a bus garage, and the original brick frontage on Pennington Street survives behind a later canopy.
